headline: 文化圈今日五四三
context: 藝文圈今天內容比較雜，一次涵蓋書市、電影、紀錄片、音樂和劇場五件事，其中一件跟台灣有關。作家匡靈秀的新書《Taipei Story》，寫一位美籍華裔學生到台灣學中文，展開一段自我發現與家族祕密的旅程。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Venice film festival The Venice fixture plays an illustrator haunted by his boyhood in Mario Martone’s part spooky, part sentimental oddity It’s always good to see the veteran Italian star Toni Servillo at Venice; in fact, the festival is pretty much unthinkable without him. But this initially promising prospect – adapted from a novel by Domenico Starnone – is a minor, quibbling tonal oddity, unsure if it wants to be scary or sentimental. Servillo lends it as much gravitas as he can: his mere presence is valuable ballast and the streetscape scenes of Naples are handled with a connoisseur’s touch by director Mario Martone, whose previous Naples-set movie Nostalgia was far superior. Daniele (played by Servillo) is a septuagenarian book illustrator whose old-fashioned, hand-drawn artistry is something he testily treasures. He has come back to his family home in Naples, to the gloomy apartment where he was brought up, just behind the train station, and where his grownup daughter Betta (Serena Rossi) now lives with her husband and their five-year-old son Mario (newcomer Lorenzo Perrotta), who is adorable and as bright as a button, but also borderline insufferable. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: An American Chinese student studies Mandarin in Taiwan, in this heartfelt journey of self-discovery and family secrets What is Taiwan? A former Japanese colony? A centre of the semiconductor industry? A democracy overseen by American imperialism? China’s next military target? An island of Austronesian Indigenous tribes? Is Taipei a cultural emblem of Taiwan, or just another booming global capital out of touch with the rest of the country? What stories will Lily Chen, an American Chinese student at Yale and Rebecca F Kuang’s funny and deadpan protagonist in Taipei Story, discover in this melting pot while spending 10 weeks learning Mandarin? A prolific maverick with rare satirical wit, Kuang has built a career debunking authoritative institutions. Babel (2022) highlights the prejudices of the British empire through a fantastical Oxford translation institute; Yellowface (2023) transplants a heist thriller into the dark heart of American publishing; Katabasis (2025), a journey into the underworld, gives the academic inferno at Cambridge a new lease of death. Centring on a tough Mandarin language school, Taipei Story explores the torture, hilarity and pretension of learning a second language, but here Kuang also offers a heartfelt journey of self-discovery and family wounds. sources.summary: Eileen and Keen Umbehr were convinced the wrong person was convicted for double-homicide. After sending Pulitzer-winning journalist Joe Sexton 2,714 emails about it, he agreed to investigate – and it led to a messy entanglement HBO is no stranger to true crime, though its offerings tend to be more prestige than your average, with documentaries such as the unrelenting sex cult nightmare The Vow and The Yogurt Shop Murders , a measured reinvestigation into the deaths of four teenage girls in Texas in the 90s. They have form, too, in drily funny sagas, such as McMillions , about a high-stakes conspiracy to fix the McDonald’s Monopoly promotion. Rarely are their documentaries both solemn and bizarro, with the exception perhaps of The Jinx. An unnerving tale of millionaire real estate heir turned convicted murderer Robert Durst, it occasionally lingered on the stranger points of his story, like the time he shoplifted a $6 sandwich for kicks. All this makes sense, really: it’s not like most homicides lend themselves to a deadpan retelling. A Killer Story is not laugh-out-loud funny, either. But this very meta three-parter manages to tell not one but two killer stories, one disturbing and the other absurd. The first concerns a woman, Dana Chandler, who is sentenced to life in prison for the murder of her ex-husband and his new girlfriend. The second is about a true crime-obsessed stranger, Eileen Umbehr, who becomes fixated on the case, spamming a journalist with tips. The emails from Umbehr were, says Joe Sexton – previously of the New York Times and investigative newsroom ProPublica – “a crazy assortment of shit … I [didn’t] know whether to call the cops on her or fucking hire her!” Continue reading...
sources.title: A Killer Story review – this tale of two relentless armchair detectives is prestige true crime

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: (Reprise) The 80-year-old continues his tireless output, delving into the past for inspiration to variable results – though two lengthy brand-new songs are real showstoppers You can’t fault Neil Young for his industry. Second Song is his second new album of 2026: the first, a double live set called As Time Explodes, was released just over three months ago. Indeed, at 80, his work schedule seems mind-boggling. Since 2020, he’s released nine new albums, a 30-minute EP, five self-directed films and three more films directed by others, 10 archival live albums, six archival studio albums and two immense box sets. He has embarked on tours with his longstanding backing band Crazy Horse, his recently convened backing band the Chrome Hearts, and solo. He has gone to public war with Spotify, Amazon, Ticketmaster and – briefly – the BBC’s coverage of Glastonbury, and penned umpteen op-ed pieces about politics, the environment and corporate media for his online newspaper the Times-Contrarian. When he recently cancelled a European tour citing exhaustion, it was hard not to think: well, I’m not surprised. You do find yourself wondering if his workload is such a good thing: not just for an elderly gentleman’s health but also for the quality of his output. Young has always prized spontaneity over finesse, but some of his more recent releases have suggested that at least a soupçon of finesse might not go amiss. Last year’s Talkin to the Trees, however, seemed to cross the line that separates the instinctive from the dashed off. Young frequently sounded as if he was making the material up as he went along, with nugatory results: “When today has come and gone, I might be singing my new song,” he offered on Family Life. “Might be short, it might be long, but I’ll be singing my new song.” If some of the melodies sounded familiar, that’s because they were. Not one but two tracks echoed the tune of Woody Guthrie’s This Land Is Your Land; First Fire of Winter was essentially Young’s 1970 masterpiece Helpless with different lyrics; Thankful rewrote 1992’s Harvest Moon. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Stephen Joseph theatre, Scarborough The playwright explores our relationship with technology, asks if robots have souls and even questions the value of art in this sci-fi courtroom drama For play number 92, Alan Ayckbourn returns to his preoccupation of exploring where we as a species are heading through a science-fiction lens. He goes back to the future. In The Trial of Romeo Oscar, the playwright famed for his domestic comedies looks to the year 2194 when humans have spread about the galaxy and androids live alongside us. One of them, RSDO83, is on trial for the murder of a teenage girl in his charge. This is Ayckbourn philosophising about the future of humanity as we sit at an obvious inflection point, asking what this moment in our relationship with technology means and where it will lead us. The questions running through the play are manifold, complex and echo those asked by sci-fi writers for decades: can robots hurt humans? Do they have souls? He is also questioning the value of art and even its purpose. Continue reading...

thread_text:
🇹🇼 台灣相關 ——

先看書市。作家匡靈秀（Rebecca F. Kuang）推出新書《Taipei Story》，寫一位美籍華裔學生到台灣學中文，展開一段自我發現與家族祕密的旅程，書裡也拋出「台灣到底是什麼」的大哉問——是曾經的日本殖民地，還是半導體重鎮。

再看電影。威尼斯影展的新片《Scherzetto》裡，資深演員托尼·塞維洛飾演一位被童年往事纏繞的插畫家，導演馬里歐·馬爾托內把它拍成半靈異、半溫情的奇特故事。

紀錄片方面，《A Killer Story》講一對夫妻艾琳與金恩·安貝爾，堅信一起雙屍命案抓錯了人，鍥而不捨寄了兩千七百多封信給普立茲獎記者喬·賽克斯頓，最後真的說動他重新調查。

音樂上，八十歲的尼爾·楊發了新專輯《Chrome Hearts: Second Song》，整體評價普通，但裡面兩首篇幅較長的新歌被認為是亮點。

劇場最後一件事，艾克鵬的新劇《The Trial of Romeo Oscar》在英國斯卡波羅上演，讓一具被控謀殺的機器人受審，順便問了問機器人有沒有靈魂、藝術還有沒有價值。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian，2026 年 9 月 11 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text: 藝文這邊今天內容比較雜，一次講五件事，其中一件跟台灣有關。先說書市，作家匡靈秀寫了一本新書，內容是一位美籍華裔學生到台灣學中文，展開一段自我發現與家族祕密的旅程，書裡也問了一個問題：台灣到底是什麼——是曾經的日本殖民地，還是半導體重鎮。換個話題，看電影。威尼斯影展一部新片，讓資深演員飾演一位被童年往事纏繞的插畫家，整部片半靈異、半溫情。再看紀錄片，有一對夫妻堅信一起雙屍命案抓錯了人，鍥而不捨寄了兩千七百多封信給一位記者，最後真的說動對方重新調查。音樂上，八十歲的搖滾歌手發了新專輯，整體評價普通，但裡面兩首篇幅較長的新歌被認為是亮點。最後看劇場，一齣新劇讓一具被控謀殺的機器人受審，順便問了問機器人有沒有靈魂。
